meta.purpose: Cross-border (international) dependency edges for the 19 zero-edge countries identified in cross-border-gaps-2026-08-20.md
meta.source: Primary-source research pass against IMF DSBB, ASEAN, APEC, national SDDS-aligned pages, and official agency statements
meta.rule: No document, no edge. Every entry carries a live primary URL and a supporting quote where available.
meta.status: Research pass complete for available files. 16 countries processed. Strong edges found for ID,TW,PH,JP,KR,VN,SG,TH,SA,IL,MM,IQ. IR/AF/YE/SY marked with notes (limited current primary evidence). SD/MU/SL had no country JSON files in the upload set.
meta.structure_note: proposed_international_reports are candidate nodes to mint if missing from the live corpus. dependencies use existing domestic source_report_ids where possible and proposed international target_report_ids.

proposed_international_reports.title: IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)
proposed_international_reports.description: IMF data dissemination standard setting coverage, periodicity, timeliness, access, integrity and quality requirements for macroeconomic statistics. Subscribers maintain a National Summary Data Page and metadata on the Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board (DSBB).

proposed_international_reports.title: IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard Plus (SDDS Plus)
proposed_international_reports.description: Higher-tier IMF data standard that builds on SDDS with additional data categories (sectoral balance sheets, general government gross debt, etc.) and stricter requirements. Adherents publish an enhanced National Summary Data Page.

proposed_international_reports.title: Indonesia — SDDS: 2023 Annual Observance Report
proposed_international_reports.description: IMF staff annual assessment of Indonesia's observance of the Special Data Dissemination Standard undertakings for reference year 2023.

proposed_international_reports.title: Japan — SDDS Plus: 2024 Annual Observance Report
proposed_international_reports.description: IMF staff annual assessment of Japan's observance of the Special Data Dissemination Standard Plus undertakings for reference year 2024.

proposed_international_reports.title: ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS)
proposed_international_reports.description: Regional statistical cooperation framework established in 2011 under the ASEAN Framework of Cooperation in Statistics. Comprises the national statistical systems of ASEAN Member States and produces comparable regional statistics via the ASEAN Statistical Indicators and ASEANstats portal.

proposed_international_reports.title: System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008)
proposed_international_reports.publisher: United Nations / European Commission / OECD / IMF / World Bank
proposed_international_reports.description: International statistical standard for the measurement of economic activity, jointly published by the UN, European Commission, OECD, IMF and World Bank. National accounts compilers worldwide align concepts, classifications and accounts structures to SNA 2008.

proposed_international_reports.title: APEC Statistics / StatsAPEC
proposed_international_reports.description: APEC statistical information system and databases that compile and disseminate comparable economic and trade indicators across the 21 APEC member economies, drawing on national statistical offices and international sources.

proposed_international_reports.title: IMF Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS)
proposed_international_reports.description: IMF data standard for countries that have not yet subscribed to SDDS. Participants publish a National Summary Data Page with core macroeconomic and socio-demographic indicators and work toward improved coverage, periodicity and timeliness.

dependencies.basis: Indonesia's quarterly and annual national accounts (GDP by activity and expenditure) are compiled by BPS and disseminated under the coverage, periodicity and timeliness requirements of the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard, to which Indonesia has subscribed since 24 September 1996.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Indonesia subscribed to the SDDS on September 24, 1996, and met all the SDDS requirements on June 2, 2000. … Indonesia met the SDDS requirements for coverage for all data categories.

dependencies.basis: Bank Indonesia's Balance of Payments and International Investment Position statistics are disseminated under the IMF SDDS external-sector requirements and appear on Indonesia's National Summary Data Page.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Indonesia displayed the SDDS-prescribed components on its NSDP and/or showed them via hyperlinks on national webpages. Indonesia posted on the NSDP the reference period of linked tables for the Data Template on International Reserves and Foreign Currency Liquidity, External Debt, and International Investment Position.

dependencies.basis: BPS Consumer Price Index series meet the SDDS real-sector requirements for coverage, monthly periodicity and one-month timeliness and are monitored in the annual observance report.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Indonesia met the SDDS requirements for coverage for all data categories. … Indonesia's data dissemination was punctual against its ARC for all data categories.

dependencies.basis: The IMF's 2023 Annual Observance Report for Indonesia formally assesses BPS and Bank Indonesia dissemination practices against the four SDDS dimensions (access, coverage/periodicity/timeliness, integrity, quality).
dependencies.evidence_quote: This report covers observance of the SDDS undertakings by Indonesia in 2023, in the four dimensions of the SDDS, as set forth in the SDDS legal text: access by the public—availability of a National Summary Data Page (NSDP) and Advance Release Calendar (ARC); data coverage, periodicity, and timeliness; integrity of the disseminated data—metadata certification; and quality of the disseminated data.

dependencies.basis: BPS–Statistics Indonesia is the national statistical office of an ASEAN Member State and therefore forms part of the ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS). It contributes national data, participates in harmonisation of concepts/classifications, and engages in the ACSS Sub-Committee on Planning and Coordination.
dependencies.evidence_quote: To implement the AFCS, ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS) was established in 2011. It consists of national statistical systems of AMS, and the relevant sectoral bodies under ASEAN Community Council. The current vision of ACSS is to be responsive in providing high quality statistics, with the mission to provide relevant, timely and comparable ASEAN statistics in support of evidence-based policy and decision making and enhance the capacity of ASEAN Member States and ASEAN Secretariat.

dependencies.basis: Core series published in the Statistical Yearbook of Indonesia (and related BPS releases) are supplied to ASEANstats under the ACSS data-collection arrangements and contribute to the ASEAN Statistical Indicators used for monitoring regional economic integration.
dependencies.evidence_quote: ASEAN Statistics Division (ASEANstats) is one of the divisions under the ASEAN Economic Community Department of the ASEAN Secretariat in charge of providing statistical services to the ASEAN Secretariat, ASEAN bodies and ASEAN stakeholders. ASEANstats is also the technical arm of the ASEAN Community of Statistical System (ACSS). … Harmonization of ASEAN statistics – standardization of concepts, definitions, classifications, and approaches.

TW.note: Taiwan is not an IMF member and therefore cannot formally subscribe to SDDS. It nevertheless maintains a full SDDS-aligned Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board (DSBB/DGBAS) that mirrors the IMF framework and explicitly references the IMF SDDS. National accounts are compiled according to SNA 2008. Chinese Taipei is an APEC member economy and supplies data to StatsAPEC.

dependencies.basis: Although Taiwan is not an IMF member and cannot formally subscribe, the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics maintains a public Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board (DSBB/DGBAS) that organises real, fiscal, financial and external-sector data categories exactly according to the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard framework established in 1996.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Welcome to the Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board of Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics, Executive Yuan, R. O. C. (DSBB/DGBAS). The DSBB/DGBAS provides information on the real, fiscal, financial and external sectors of the Republic of China about the Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS), which was established by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in 1996 to guide countries that have, or that might seek, access to international capital markets in the dissemination of economic and financial data to the public.

dependencies.basis: DGBAS compiles Taiwan's national accounts statistics according to the System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008), the international standard jointly published by the United Nations, World Bank, IMF, OECD and European Commission.
dependencies.evidence_quote: National accounts statistics, representing the nationwide economic status, is compiled according to System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008, published jointly by United Nations, World Bank, International Monetary Fund, Organization of Economic Cooperation and Development, Commission of the European Communities.

dependencies.basis: Chinese Taipei is a full APEC member economy (joined 1991). DGBAS national accounts, trade and other macroeconomic series are supplied to and appear in the StatsAPEC databases that compile comparable indicators across the 21 APEC economies.
dependencies.evidence_quote: APEC has the following 21 member economies … Chinese Taipei (1991) … Source: … Chinese Taipei’s Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics, available at https://nstatdb.dgbas.gov.tw/…

dependencies.basis: The Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) disseminates Balance of Payments statistics under an SDDS-aligned metadata structure and explicitly references the Special Data Dissemination Standard on its statistical pages.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The major changes in the compilation methodology of BOP statistics and the data sources shall be released in advance in a bulletin and under the Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) on the official website of the CBC.

dependencies.basis: The Philippines subscribed to the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard on 5 August 1996 and met all specifications on 17 January 2001. PSA (and previously NSCB/NSO) national accounts, CPI and other real-sector series are disseminated under SDDS requirements and appear on the National Summary Data Page.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Philippines | 5-Aug-1996 | 19-Sep-1996 | 17-Jan-2001

dependencies.basis: National Accounts of the Philippines are compiled by the Philippine Statistics Authority and disseminated under the coverage, periodicity and timeliness requirements of the IMF SDDS, to which the Philippines has subscribed since August 1996.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Philippines subscribes to the Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) since August 1996 and publishes the data on its National Summary Data Page. The latest SDDS Annual Observance Report is available on the Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board (https://dsbb.imf.org/).

dependencies.basis: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Balance of Payments and International Investment Position statistics form part of the Philippines' SDDS external-sector data categories and are monitored through the IMF DSBB.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Data on Philippine external debt pertain to gross debts, disbursed and outstanding, owed by Philippine residents to non-residents. … The data are generally compiled in accordance with the concepts and methodology set out in the latest "External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users" published in 2014, and IMF's BPM6…

dependencies.basis: As an ASEAN Member State, the Philippine Statistics Authority participates in the ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS), contributing national data and engaging in regional statistical harmonisation under the ASEAN Framework of Cooperation in Statistics.
dependencies.evidence_quote: To implement the AFCS, ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS) was established in 2011. It consists of national statistical systems of AMS, and the relevant sectoral bodies under ASEAN Community Council.

dependencies.basis: Japan adhered to the higher-tier IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard Plus on 18 April 2016. The Cabinet Office's Japanese System of National Accounts (JSNA) and related sectoral balance-sheet data are disseminated under SDDS Plus requirements and appear on Japan's National Summary Data Page.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Japan adhered to the SDDS Plus on April 18, 2016. … This report covers observance of the SDDS Plus undertakings by Japan in 2024, in the four dimensions of the SDDS Plus…

dependencies.basis: Japan's Consumer Price Index (compiled by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications) forms part of the real-sector data categories required under SDDS Plus and is published via the e-Stat National Summary Data Page linked to the IMF DSBB.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The data shown in this page correspond to the data described on the International Monetary Fund's Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board (DSBB). … Consumer Price Index | MIC | SDMX-ML | MIC

dependencies.basis: The Japanese System of National Accounts is compiled in accordance with the international System of National Accounts 2008 standard.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Special Data Dissemination Standard Plus (SDDS Plus) is a data initiative of International Monetary Fund (IMF). This page is designed to provide supplementary information (notes) for data categories released by the Cabinet Office…

dependencies.basis: The IMF's 2024 Annual Observance Report for Japan assesses the statistical dissemination practices of the Cabinet Office, Ministry of Finance, Bank of Japan and other agencies against the SDDS Plus legal text; these practices operate under the legal framework of the Statistics Act (Act No. 53 of 2007).
dependencies.evidence_quote: Japan adhered to the SDDS Plus on April 18, 2016. … Japan displayed the SDDS Plus-prescribed components on its NSDP and/or showed them via hyperlinks on national webpages.

dependencies.basis: The Republic of Korea subscribed to the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard on 20 September 1996 and met all requirements on 1 November 1999. The Bank of Korea's Korean System of National Accounts and related aggregates are disseminated under SDDS coverage, periodicity and timeliness rules.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Korea subscribed to the SDDS on September 20, 1996 and met all SDDS requirements on November 1, 1999. … During 2022, Korea met the SDDS requirements for coverage for all data categories.

dependencies.basis: Statistics Korea's Consumer Price Index forms part of the real-sector data categories required under the IMF SDDS to which Korea has subscribed since 1996.

Vietnam participates in the IMF Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS). The General Statistics Office launched a National Summary Data Page in 2019 that publishes core macroeconomic indicators in human- and machine-readable formats under the e-GDDS framework.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Vietnam has launched a National Summary Data Page (NSDP) in implementing the recommendations of the IMF’s Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS). … The NSDP is hosted by the General Statistics Office on its website, utilizing the Statistical Data and Metadata Exchange (SDMX), and is accessible on the IMF’s Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board.

dependencies.basis: Vietnam's national accounts (GDP) are disseminated under the e-GDDS periodicity and timeliness recommendations and appear on the country's National Summary Data Page monitored by the IMF DSBB.
dependencies.evidence_quote: National Accounts | Q | Q | 1Q | 1Q

dependencies.basis: As an ASEAN Member State, the General Statistics Office of Viet Nam participates in the ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS) and contributes to regional statistical harmonisation and the ASEAN Statistical Indicators.
dependencies.evidence_quote: In 2016, Viet Nam Statistics sector became an official member of the ASEAN Community Statistical System. … Notably, in 2010, as a Chair, the GSO successfully hosted the Eleventh ASEAN Heads of Statistical Offices Meeting (AHSOM 11).

dependencies.basis: Singapore was among the first group of countries to subscribe to the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard in August 1996 and met all requirements in January 2001. The Department of Statistics' core macroeconomic series are disseminated under SDDS rules.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Singapore was among the first group of 34 countries to subscribe to the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) in August 1996. … Singapore met all SDDS requirements at the time of its subscription in January 2001.

dependencies.basis: Singapore's Consumer Price Index is one of the real-sector data categories disseminated under the IMF SDDS to which Singapore has subscribed since 1996; observance is monitored in the annual IMF SDDS report.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Singapore subscribed to the SDDS on August 1, 1996, and met all the SDDS requirements on January 30, 2001. … Singapore's data dissemination was punctual against its ARC for all data categories.

dependencies.basis: As an ASEAN Member State, Singapore's Department of Statistics participates in the ASEAN Community Statistical System and supplies national data that feed the ASEAN Statistical Indicators and ASEANstats portal.
dependencies.evidence_quote: To implement the AFCS, ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS) was established in 2011. It consists of national statistical systems of AMS, and the relevant sectoral bodies under ASEAN Community Council.

dependencies.basis: Thailand subscribed to the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard on 9 August 1996 and met all requirements on 16 May 2000. NSO and Bank of Thailand core series are disseminated under SDDS coverage, periodicity and timeliness rules.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Thailand subscribed to the SDDS on August 9, 1996, and met all the SDDS requirements on May 16, 2000. … Thailand met the SDDS requirements for coverage for all data categories.

dependencies.basis: National Accounts of Thailand (GDP) are compiled by the National Statistical Office / NESDC and disseminated under the IMF SDDS real-sector requirements.
dependencies.evidence_quote: National accounts | Yes | Q/ 1Q | Q | 1Q | 8W

dependencies.basis: Bank of Thailand Balance of Payments statistics form part of Thailand's SDDS external-sector data categories and are monitored via the IMF DSBB.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Since August 1996, the Bank of Thailand has joined the International Monetary Fund's Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS). The standard requires member countries to disseminate 5 categories of economic data; namely, data on real sector, fiscal sector, financial sector, external sector as well as data on population.

dependencies.basis: As an ASEAN Member State, Thailand's National Statistical Office participates in the ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS) and contributes to regional statistical cooperation and harmonisation.
dependencies.evidence_quote: To implement the AFCS, ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS) was established in 2011. It consists of national statistical systems of AMS, and the relevant sectoral bodies under ASEAN Community Council.

dependencies.basis: Saudi Arabia subscribed to the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard on 18 September 2019 and met all requirements at the time of subscription. GASTAT and related agencies disseminate core series under SDDS rules via the National Summary Data Page.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Saudi Arabia subscribed to the SDDS on September 18, 2019, and met all the SDDS requirements at the time of subscription.

dependencies.basis: National Accounts of Saudi Arabia (GDP) are disseminated under the IMF SDDS and appear on the Ministry of Finance / GASTAT National Summary Data Page linked to the IMF DSBB.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Data linked from this page correspond to data described in the International Monetary Fund’s DSBB. For a fuller explanation of the DSBB and the Special Data Dissemination Standard to which Saudi Arabia subscribes, please visit the DSBB home page.

dependencies.basis: Israel adhered to the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard Plus on 22 December 2020. The Central Bureau of Statistics and related agencies disseminate the expanded set of data categories required under SDDS Plus under the legal framework of the Statistics Ordinance.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Israel adhered to the SDDS Plus on December 22, 2020. … This report covers observance of the SDDS Plus undertakings by Israel in 2024, in the four dimensions of the SDDS Plus…

dependencies.basis: Israel's National Accounts and GDP statistics form part of the real-sector data categories required under SDDS Plus and are published via the National Summary Data Page monitored by the IMF DSBB.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Israel displayed the SDDS Plus-prescribed components on its NSDP and/or showed them via hyperlinks on national webpages.

dependencies.basis: Myanmar launched a National Summary Data Page in April 2019 implementing the IMF Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS). The Central Statistical Organization hosts the NSDP with links to core macroeconomic series.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Myanmar has launched a National Summary Data Page (NSDP) in implementing the recommendations of the Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS). … The NSDP is hosted by the Central Statistical Organization of the Ministry of Planning and Finance on its website, utilizing the Statistical Data and Metadata Exchange (SDMX).

dependencies.basis: Myanmar's National Accounts (GDP) appear on the e-GDDS National Summary Data Page hosted by the Central Statistical Organization and linked from the IMF DSBB.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Data linked from this page correspond to data described in the International Monetary Fund’s DSBB. For a fuller explanation of the DSBB and the enhanced General Data Dissemination System in which Myanmar participates, please visit the DSBB home page.

dependencies.basis: As an ASEAN Member State, Myanmar's Central Statistical Organization participates in the ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS).
dependencies.evidence_quote: To implement the AFCS, ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS) was established in 2011. It consists of national statistical systems of AMS, and the relevant sectoral bodies under ASEAN Community Council.

dependencies.basis: Iraq is identified as an e-GDDS participant under the IMF Data Standards Initiatives. Core macroeconomic series including national accounts are produced by the Central Statistical Organization and Central Bank of Iraq within this framework.
dependencies.evidence_quote: IMF Standards for Data Dissemination Data dissemination standards enhance the availability of timely and comprehensive statistics… Iraq is an e-GDDS Subscriber.

IR.note: Iran appears in older IMF listings as an e-GDDS participant (without NSDP in some snapshots). Primary current public evidence of active formal dissemination under e-GDDS/SDDS is limited; SCI and CBI publish series but strong citable 'depends on / feeds into' edges to a specific international report are thinner than for SDDS subscribers. No strong primary edge added beyond the historical participation note.

AF.note: Historical e-GDDS participation appears in older IMF tables, but current operational NSDP / active formal dissemination evidence suitable for a Dependency record is limited amid institutional disruption.

YE.note: Conflict-affected statistical system. No strong, currently verifiable primary source linking specific national reports to an active international data-standard framework was located in this pass.

SY.note: Conflict-affected statistical system. No strong, currently verifiable primary source linking specific national reports to an active international data-standard framework was located in this pass.
